messages:
ops-bot: Pager alert — kv-cache miss rate jumped to 48% and Batching stalls observed on /v1/complete (funcall-heavy). Link: https://grafana.redwood/uid/kv-cache-dash?panel=12 :rotating_light:

jamal: seeing sustained >500ms tail latencies and lots of batch fragmentation. toolcall requests show lots of structured output arrays that blow KV key prefixes.

mina: customer reports: "generation timeouts" for chattool customers, error rate 5x for a subset of requests hitting structured tool outputs. CS is getting multiple tickets.

taylor: @jamal can you confirm this is correlated to the structured-output rollout from earlier today? any config changes?

jamal: yes — we merged funcall-prefetch flag + new structured serializer at 10:14; traffic pattern changed -> many unique prefixes -> KV cache blowup -> batching degenerates because shard occupancy low.

alex: repro logs:
```
2026-03-15T20:07:02Z svc-runtime[pid=3982]: evict_threshold=0.12 current_keys=2.1M prefix_entropy=0.93
2026-03-15T20:07:03Z svc-runtime[pid=3982]: batch_queue_len=120 stalled_shards=18 avg_batch_tokens=6
2026-03-15T20:07:04Z svc-runtime[pid=3982]: funcall: serialized_struct length=4096 unique_prefix=true
```

mina: impact matrix from CS: ~17 customers affected (mostly PLG + some small Prod). p95 latency jumped from 280ms -> 2.4s on affected flows. 502s and 504s for very long tails.

jamal: quick mitigation ideas: 1) toggle off funcall-prefetch to stop chaotic prefetching, 2) bump min_batch_tokens to avoid tiny batches, 3) apply prefix-hash cap for structured-output serializer.

taylor: agree. Let's do low-risk first: flip funcall-prefetch to false for hosted pool A (the one with most traffic).

alex: commands to flip via k8s-config: 
```
# turn off prefetch for pool A
curl -X POST https://config.redwood/api/pools/A/actions -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CFG' -d '{"funcall_prefetch":false}'
```

jamal: deploying now to pool A canary (3 nodes) — rolling patch.

ops-bot: Deploy started by jamal at 2026-03-15T20:12:40Z — config change id cfg-20260315-198

taylor: monitoring graph — within 2 minutes miss rate dropped to 22% :slightly_smiling_face:

mina: CS update sent: "We've identified a regression related to structured function outputs; we deployed an emergency config to reduce customer impact. We'll follow up with RCA." Customers acknowledged.

jamal: second mitigation: bump min_batch_tokens from 1 -> 8 for the small pooling group. This prevents the runtime from creating tiny batches that increase per-token cost and amplify fragmentation.

alex: doing config change for min_batch_tokens in hosted-global: 
```
kubectl -n svc apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: serving-batching
data:
  min_batch_tokens: "8"
EOF
```

ops-bot: Configmap update started — will roll to 12 nodes (staged)

jamal: after both changes p95 dropped to 380ms and miss-rate ~9%. still monitoring for any regressions.

taylor: also scheduling follow-up hotfix: serializer will be changed to emit stable prefix tokens for structured arrays — dev oncall will push patch tomorrow.

mina: customers asking for timeline for full fix — we told them 24 hours for a proper rollout.

alex: note: we also disabled aggressive eviction in pool B earlier which made things worse — reverted that before the canary. Revert command:
```
# revert eviction policy
curl -X POST https://config.redwood/api/pools/B/actions -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CFG' -d '{"eviction_aggressive":false}'
```

jamal: logs after canary:
```
2026-03-15T20:20:01Z svc-runtime[pid=5781]: batch_queue_len=30 avg_batch_tokens=9 miss_rate=0.09
2026-03-15T20:20:02Z svc-runtime[pid=5781]: tail_latency_p95=0.38s
```

taylor: good. We should also clear a small percentage of highly-saturated prefixes from the KV cache to reclaim memory — run prefix-prune script with dry-run first.

alex: running dry-run now: `python tools/prefix_prune.py --pool A --dry-run` output: 23k prefixes candidate -> would reclaim ~1.2GB.

jamal: schedule actual prune at 00:30 UTC when traffic lower. will coordinate with oncall handoff.

ops-bot: Incident update: mitigation applied, partial recovery. Severity downgraded from Sev2 -> Sev3 at 2026-03-15T20:35:00Z.

mina: CS: consolidated customer list — 17 impacted, 4 had retries fail (escalated). We're offering 1 week credit per affected customer as a gesture. Legal looped in.

taylor: prepping RCA notes. primary cause: structured-output serializer increased prefix cardinality; secondary: new prefetch logic and aggressive eviction combined to amplify shard fragmentation. Fix path: serializer change + config guardrails + improved telemetry.

jamal: handing off to night SRE oncall @sre-oncall for monitoring and prune at 00:30 UTC. leaving runbook snippet below.

jamal: Runbook (short):
1) monitor grafana 'kv-cache/miss-rate' panel
2) if miss_rate > 0.2 -> flip funcall_prefetch false for remaining pools
3) if tail_p95 > 1s -> increase min_batch_tokens to 16
4) run prefix_prune for pool A (single step) then monitor memory and miss rate

sre-oncall: acknowledged — I'll take this at 2026-03-15T21:02:15Z. will report back after prune.

taylor: thanks all. postmortem owner: jamal. target for RCA in 5 business days.

mina: adding notes to incident doc: https://confluence.redwood/infra/incidents/1978524321

ops-bot: Incident closed for active mitigation (monitor-only) — next update expected after night prune.

sre-oncall: PRUNE done at 2026-03-16T00:46Z — reclaimed 1.1GB, p95 stable at 360ms, miss_rate 0.07. closing handoff.

mina: final CS template ready, prep to send tomorrow morning.

jamal: thanks team. putting RCA draft in /shared/rca/1978524321-draft.md

alex: :thumbsup:
